section.title: Python vs Java — Advanced
section.subtitle: OOP, functional programming, decorators, generators, modules, virtual environments, JSON and APIs.

python.definition: class defines an object blueprint; __init__ is the constructor; self refers to the instance. Inheritance via class Child(Parent), polymorphism via method overriding.

java.definition: class defines the blueprint; constructor has the class name; this refers to the instance. Inheritance via extends; polymorphism via @Override methods.

topics.title: Encapsulation
topics.learn: Public, protected, private conventions — hiding internal data.

python.definition: No true private keyword — convention uses a single underscore _attr (protected-ish) or double underscore __attr (name-mangled). @property gives getter/setter behaviour.

java.definition: private fields with public getter/setter methods enforce encapsulation strictly at compile time.

topics.title: Abstraction
topics.learn: Abstract classes and methods — defining interfaces without full implementation.

python.definition: Python has no abstract keyword — use abc.ABC and @abstractmethod to force subclasses to implement methods.

java.definition: abstract class + abstract method — subclasses MUST implement abstract methods. Cannot instantiate the abstract class directly.

topics.title: Lambda / Anonymous Functions
topics.learn: Anonymous functions — small functions defined inline.

python.definition: lambda args: expression creates a small anonymous function. Limited to a single expression.
python.code:
square = lambda x: x * x
add = lambda a, b: a + b

print(square(5))        # 25
print(add(3, 4))         # 7

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]
doubled = list(map(lambda x: x * 2, nums))
print(doubled)           # [2, 4, 6, 8]

java.definition: Lambda expressions (params) -> expression. Java lambdas need a functional interface (SAM).

topics.title: Map & Filter
topics.learn: Functional programming — transforming and selecting data.

python.definition: map(func, iterable) applies func to every item; filter(func, iterable) keeps items where func returns True.
python.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

squared = list(map(lambda x: x * x, nums))
evens = list(filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, nums))

print(squared)   # [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36]
print(evens)     # [2, 4, 6]

java.definition: Stream API: stream().map() and stream().filter() with lambda expressions, collected via Collectors.

topics.title: List Comprehension
topics.learn: Shorter list operations — create lists in one expression.

python.definition: [expr for item in iterable if condition] builds a list compactly — combines loop + filter + transform.
python.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

squares = [x * x for x in nums]
evens = [x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]
labels = [f"num-{x}" for x in nums[:3]]

print(squares)  # [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36]
print(evens)    # [2, 4, 6]
print(labels)   # ['num-1', 'num-2', 'num-3']

java.definition: No direct equivalent — use Stream API (map/filter/collect) which serves the same purpose.

topics.title: Decorators
topics.learn: Modifying function behaviour without changing the function.

python.definition: A decorator is a function that takes another function and returns a wrapped version — used with @syntax above the function.

java.definition: No decorator syntax — achieved via AOP (AspectJ / Spring @Aspect) or wrapper/delegate patterns.

topics.title: Generators
topics.learn: Yield and lazy iteration — produce values one at a time.

python.definition: A function with yield returns a generator — values are produced lazily on demand, saving memory.

java.definition: No yield — Java uses Iterator/Stream API for lazy evaluation. Iterators produce elements on demand.

python.definition: A module is a .py file; packages are folders with __init__.py. import module / from module import name.
python.code:
# mymodule.py
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello {name}"

# main.py
import mymodule
from mymodule import greet

print(mymodule.greet("Sam"))
print(greet("Sam"))

java.definition: Packages organise classes into folders matching the package name. import com.example.Utils; — one public class per file.

topics.title: Virtual Environments
topics.learn: venv and pip — isolated Python environments.

python.definition: venv creates an isolated folder with its own Python + packages. pip installs packages inside it. Java uses build tools (Maven/Gradle) instead.
python.code:
# Create & activate (macOS/Linux)
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install packages
pip install requests flask

# Deactivate
deactivate

# Java equivalent: Maven downloads deps into ~/.m2
# mvn dependency:get -Dartifact=requests:requests:2.0

java.definition: Java doesn't use virtualenvs — dependencies are managed by Maven (pom.xml) or Gradle (build.gradle), downloaded into a shared local repo (~/.m2).
java.code:
<!-- pom.xml dependency example -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
</dependency>

<!-- Then: mvn spring-boot:run -->

python.definition: json module: json.dumps() converts Python objects to JSON string; json.loads() parses JSON to Python objects. dict/list map directly.
python.code:
import json

data = {"name": "Priya", "age": 20, "marks": [90, 85]}

# Python -> JSON
json_str = json.dumps(data, indent=2)
print(json_str)

# JSON -> Python
parsed = json.loads(json_str)
print(parsed["name"])   # Priya

# File I/O
with open("data.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f)

java.definition: Jackson (or Gson) serialises Java objects to JSON and back. Spring Boot includes Jackson automatically.

python.definition: requests library: requests.get()/post() return Response objects with .json(), .status_code, .text.
python.code:
import requests

# GET
resp = requests.get("https://api.github.com/users/octocat")
print(resp.status_code)          # 200
print(resp.json()["login"])      # octocat

# POST with JSON body
resp = requests.post("https://httpbin.org/post",
                    json={"key": "value"})
print(resp.json())

java.definition: Java 11+ HttpClient, or Spring's RestTemplate/WebClient. Response body parsed via Jackson.
